meta.note: Only people and organisations that actually operationalised AGI: a stated criterion concrete enough to check. Definitions with no threshold or measurement procedure are excluded. Entries marked claim=proxy are widely read as AGI progress indicators but were never framed as AGI tests by their authors; they are listed separately on the page.

definitions.name: The Turing Test
definitions.quote: an average interrogator will not have more than 70 per cent chance of making the right identification after five minutes of questioning
definitions.status_today: Passed in 2025, against a bar Turing never set. The 70% figure was his prediction for the year 2000, not a stated pass mark; the field retrofitted it into one. Scored against that retrofitted bar: Jones and Bergen ran two randomised, pre-registered three-party tests at UC San Diego, in which participants held simultaneous five-minute conversations with one human and one system, then judged which was which. GPT-4.5 with a humanlike-persona prompt was judged to be the human 73% of the time, selected as human significantly more often than the actual human participants. Two caveats keep this honest: the pass is prompt-dependent, and the same model without the persona prompt does not pass. The most famous test in the field fell to a system two generations behind the frontier.
definitions.verification_note: Peer-reviewed PNAS study, pre-registered, no lab involvement

definitions.name: The Coffee Test
definitions.quote: a machine to enter an average American home and figure out how to make coffee
definitions.quote_source: Steve Wozniak. Find the machine, the coffee, a mug and water, and operate an unfamiliar appliance, in a house it has never seen
definitions.status_today: Not passed. No robot has entered an unfamiliar home, found the kitchen, the coffee and a mug, and worked out an appliance it had never seen. The useful number is METR's: time horizons on visual computer-use tasks run 40 to 100 times shorter than on software-engineering tasks, and METR put Claude Sonnet 4.5's real-world coffee-making horizon at about two minutes. Elsewhere the picture agrees. Simulated robotic manipulation succeeds 89.4% of the time while real household tasks run at 12%. Kitchen demonstrations from Figure, 1X and Physical Intelligence are real but instrumented or trained. Nobody has done it cold in a stranger's house.
definitions.verification_note: Never attempted in an unfamiliar home; scored from METR's physical time-horizon proxy

definitions.name: 85% on ARC-AGI-2
definitions.progress_note: 24% on the set the prize uses
definitions.quote: Can you create a system that can reach 85% accuracy?
definitions.quote_source: ARC Prize Foundation, 2025. The prize is scored on the private set, inside a compute-limited offline container.
definitions.status_today: ARC-AGI-2 has two scores and the gap between them is the whole story. On the semi-private set, which frontier API models are evaluated against, GPT-5.6 Sol reaches 92.5% and Claude Opus 5 reaches 90.4%. Six configurations now clear the 85% bar. On the private set, inside the compute-limited offline container the prize actually uses, the record is 24% and unclaimed. The 68-point gap says something specific: current systems clear the bar by spending money, at $1.44 to $2.06 per task. Efficiency was the entire point of Chollet's definition, and it is the half that has not moved. ARC Prize 2026 offers $2M across three tracks and closes to submissions on 2 November, with results on 4 December, so this may resolve before the year ends.
definitions.verification_note: Adjudicated inside ARC Prize's own Kaggle competition
definitions.claim_note: Chollet has said plainly that solving ARC-AGI would not mean AGI had been achieved. The prize is framed as a necessary milestone, not a finish line.

definitions.name: ARC-AGI-3: interactive novel environments
definitions.quote: An interactive reasoning benchmark which challenges AI agents to explore novel environments, acquire goals on the fly, build adaptable world models, and learn continuously.
definitions.quote_source: ARC Prize Foundation, launched 25 March 2026. A 100% score means agents beat every environment as efficiently as humans.
definitions.status_today: The cleanest AGI gap number currently available: 30% against a human 100%. Agents get no instructions, no rules and no stated goals. They must explore, infer how the environment works, work out what winning looks like, and carry what they learn forward. At launch in March 2026 the best frontier model scored 0.51%. Claude Opus 5, tested on 24 July, scored 30.16%, roughly four times the next best system, GPT-5.6 Sol at 7.8%, with every older frontier model still near zero. That is the largest single-step gain on any AGI-framed benchmark right now, and it is one vendor's unreplicated result. Note the cost: that run came to $20,657, so on the efficiency dimension Chollet's definition actually cares about, this is nowhere near human.
definitions.verification_note: ARC Prize tested Claude Opus 5 directly, but the result is one vendor's, unreplicated
definitions.claim_note: AGI-framed by name, but the ARC Prize Foundation claims it as a measure of one missing capability, not as a sufficient test for general intelligence.

definitions.name: The AGI Score: ten cognitive domains
definitions.affiliation: CAIS, with Bengio, Marcus, Schmidt, Tegmark and ~28 others
definitions.quote: AGI is an AI that can match or exceed the cognitive versatility and proficiency of a well-educated adult.
definitions.quote_source: "A Definition of AGI", October 2025. Grounded in Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory, the most empirically validated model of human cognition
definitions.status_today: The closest thing to a scoreboard anyone has built: ten cognitive domains, each weighted 10%, scored with adapted human psychometric batteries. GPT-4 scored 27%. GPT-5 scored 57%. The single most striking result is that both score 0% on Long-Term Memory Storage. They cannot permanently learn anything after deployment. Because domains are weighted equally, that one zero caps any current-architecture system at 90%, which makes this the strongest available argument that scaling alone cannot finish the job. Two caveats: equal weighting is a value judgement with no empirical backing, and the score is stale. No 2026 model has been run through this framework, so the most-cited number in AGI discourse is nine months and several model generations old.
definitions.verification_note: Scored by the paper's own authors and never independently replicated; no 2026 model has been run at all

definitions.name: The Hutter Prize: compression as intelligence
definitions.quote: enwik9 constitutes an amount of non-visual knowledge an average adult human holds, so compressors compressing enwik9 better than a human will predict better, and hence should be smarter... which, if achieved, most would agree constitutes AGI.
definitions.status_today: Twenty years old, still running, and the numbers are sobering. The official record is 110,793,128 bytes, set in September 2024, and across all eight winners in the prize's history €29,945 of the €500,000 pool has ever been paid out, about 6%. Here is the interpretive problem that makes this entry worth including: the best unconstrained compressor in the world is a transformer, nncp v3.2 at 106.6 MB, comfortably better than the record. It cannot win, because it violates the prize's rules limiting entrants to 50 hours on a single CPU core with 10GB of RAM. The prize was designed on the premise that compression is intelligence; when neural methods started winning at compression, the resource constraints kept them out.
definitions.verification_note: Prize committee adjudicates every award against a byte count

definitions.name: $100B in cumulative profits
definitions.progress_note: clause deleted before it could resolve
definitions.quote: systems that have the ability to generate the maximum total profits to which its earliest investors, including Microsoft, are entitled
definitions.quote_source: Reported by The Information, Dec 2024. The contract itself is not public
definitions.status_today: This definition no longer exists. The AGI clause was removed from the Microsoft–OpenAI agreement on 27 April 2026; Microsoft's announcement of the amended deal does not contain the word AGI at all. It was never triggered, and the independent expert panel created to verify it never convened. On the underlying metric, progress is negative: OpenAI reached roughly $25B annualised revenue by early 2026 while running deeply unprofitable. Three things are near-universally misreported here: the clause specified profits, not revenue; the figure was cumulative, not annual; and it was pegged to the capped-profit structure OpenAI itself dissolved in October 2025. The most falsifiable AGI definition ever written was settled by commercial renegotiation, not by anyone crossing a technical line.
definitions.verification_note: Rests on the two counterparties' own disclosures; the contract has never been public

definitions.name: Expert parity on real occupational deliverables
definitions.progress_note: parity reached on the benchmark itself
definitions.quote: a domain expert sees only the task and two unlabeled deliverables, and ranks them without knowing which is which
definitions.quote_source: GDPval, OpenAI, September 2025. 50% means indistinguishable from an industry expert.
definitions.status_today: The most rigorously built economic criterion anyone has published: 1,320 tasks across 44 occupations, drawn from real deliverables by professionals averaging 14 years' experience, graded by blind pairwise comparison against a human expert's work. Parity has been reached. The September 2025 paper put Claude Opus 4.1 at 47.6% wins-or-ties; GPT-5.2 later reached 70.9%, comfortably past the 50% parity bar. Quote these like for like: the same model's straight win rate is about 49.7%, and mixing the two metrics is the most common error made with this benchmark. Epoch AI's February 2026 verdict is the part that matters. GDPval "is falling short in its role as a leading indicator for automation." It was built to predict economic impact, it reached parity, and the impact did not follow.
definitions.verification_note: Scored by Epoch AI and Artificial Analysis, though the benchmark is OpenAI's own
definitions.claim_note: OpenAI built GDPval to measure economic task performance and never claimed parity on it constitutes AGI. Reading it as an AGI threshold is this page's inference, not OpenAI's claim.

definitions.name: The world economy growing at 10%
definitions.quote: Us self-claiming some AGI milestone, that's just nonsensical benchmark hacking to me. The real benchmark is: the world growing at 10%.
definitions.status_today: The single most unambiguous criterion in this collection: world GDP growth is measured quarterly by institutions with no stake in the AGI debate. It is also nowhere close. The IMF's April 2026 outlook projects 3.1% global growth for 2026, revised down from 3.3%; US real GDP grew 2.1% in Q1 2026. The deeper problem for AI attribution: roughly three-quarters of Q1 2026 US GDP growth came from AI capital expenditure. That is the economy building the factory, not the factory producing, and Goldman Sachs found that some $700B of 2025 global AI capex produced no measurable productivity impact. The criterion cannot distinguish AI-caused growth from any other cause; its strength is that it is immune to benchmark gaming, which was exactly Nadella's point.

evidence.label: Epoch: AI datacenter share of GDP

definitions.name: Turn $100,000 into $1,000,000
definitions.affiliation: CEO, Microsoft AI; co-founder of DeepMind
definitions.quote: Go make $1 million on a retail web platform in a few months with just a $100,000 investment.
definitions.quote_source: Mustafa Suleyman, MIT Technology Review, July 2023
definitions.status_today: Arguably the cleanest pass/fail criterion anyone has proposed: a defined stake, a defined multiple, a defined venue, a defined horizon, and a bank balance as the scorekeeper. Not passed, and no credible public claim of a pass. The nearest real evidence is Anthropic's Project Vend, where Claude ran an actual office store. Phase one lost money and was talked into buying tungsten cubes at a loss; phase two held a profit margin, and by mid-2026 had expanded to AI-run stores and cafés. In simulation, Claude Opus 4.6 averaged just over $8,000 from a $500 start on Vending-Bench 2, against an estimated strong-human strategy of about $63,000. The test is usually shortened to "turn $100K into $1M", but the original specifies on a retail web platform, which rules out the trading and crypto strategies most likely to produce a spurious pass.
definitions.verification_note: Never attempted in the real economy; scored from simulated proxies

definitions.name: Powerful AI: a country of geniuses in a datacenter
definitions.quote: It does not just passively answer questions; instead, it can be given tasks that take hours, days, or weeks to complete, and then goes off and does those tasks autonomously, in the way a smart employee would.
definitions.quote_source: Dario Amodei, "Machines of Loving Grace", October 2024
definitions.status_today: Amodei rejects the term AGI and defines "powerful AI" by the five properties listed above. Two are comfortably met. Two are partial. One cannot be tested at all, and it is the one carrying the definition: nobody has proposed a way to check whether a system is "smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most relevant fields." The autonomy clause is where the action is, because METR measures it directly. The last published frontier figure is 17.4 hours at 50% reliability, and about 3.1 hours at 80%. Hours, yes. Days, marginally. Weeks, no. The score is an unweighted mean across the five properties, which flatters the result, because Amodei states them as a conjunction where every one must hold. His 2024 essay put powerful AI "as early as 2026"; the January 2026 restatement moved that to one or two years without noting the earlier window had expired.

criteria.label: Smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most relevant fields
criteria.note: No test, no threshold, no evaluator. This is the property the whole definition rests on and the only one he never operationalized.

criteria.label: All the interfaces of a human working virtually: text, audio, video, mouse and keyboard, internet
criteria.note: Shipped across frontier models; computer-use agents are in production.

criteria.label: Runs tasks taking hours, days or weeks autonomously
criteria.note: METR's frontier 50%-reliability horizon is 17.4h, but only ~3.1h at 80%. Hours yes, days marginal, weeks no.

criteria.label: Controls physical tools, robots and lab equipment through a computer
criteria.note: Real in instrumented settings; simulated manipulation runs 89% against 12% on real household tasks.

criteria.label: Millions of parallel instances at 10-100x human speed
criteria.note: Not in doubt. GDPval measured frontier models completing expert deliverables around 100x faster.

definitions.name: Automated AI R&D: the three labs' own trigger
definitions.affiliation: written independently, in their safety frameworks
definitions.quote: recursively self improving (i.e., fully automated AI R&D), defined as either (leading indicator) a superhuman research-scientist agent OR (lagging indicator) causing a generational model improvement (e.g., from OpenAI o1 to OpenAI o3) in 1/5th the wall-clock time of equivalent progress in 2024, sustainably for several months
definitions.quote_source: OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2. The Critical threshold for AI Self-Improvement
definitions.status_today: The most adjudicable AGI definitions in existence, and all three are untriggered. Three commercial rivals, writing independently and with every incentive to claim capability, each defined a recursive-AI-R&D threshold. As of July 2026: Anthropic formally determined Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross it and published a sabotage risk report anyway because the call was difficult; OpenAI's system card for GPT-5.6 states plainly that none of the three variants reach even the High rung, two full steps below Critical; and Gemini 3.1 Pro Deep Think sits below every DeepMind CCL. Unlike benchmark scores, these are negative determinations with legal and reputational exposure attached. The obvious caveat: all three are self-assessed, and no regulator publishes an independent determination against these thresholds.
definitions.verification_note: All three determinations are made by the labs about their own models; no regulator publishes an independent finding
definitions.claim_note: These are risk-management triggers written for safety frameworks. None of the three labs says crossing one means AGI has arrived, though all three treat it as the point where progress stops being human-paced.

definitions.name: Three of five tasks, by one system
definitions.affiliation: offered to Elon Musk; criteria co-authored with Ernest Davis
definitions.progress_note: none met, three partial, of five
definitions.quote: if you (or anyone else) manages to beat at least three of them in 2029 — with a single system; three separate systems would obviously not count as general — you win; if only one or two are broken, we can't very well say we have nailed the general part in artificial general intelligence, can we?
definitions.quote_source: Gary Marcus, "Dear Elon Musk", 31 May 2022 (generality clause added June 2024)
definitions.status_today: This is an unaccepted offer, not a bet. No money has ever been at risk. Marcus offered $100,000 in May 2022; within a week Vivek Wadhwa and others had matched it to $500,000. Musk never responded, then or to the $1M and $10M offers that followed. Any description of this as "Marcus's bet with Musk" is wrong. None of the five tasks are unambiguously met by a single system, which is the bar the offer actually sets. The kitchen task is furthest away, and it is the one Marcus himself later excluded from his real wager with Miles Brundage as too dependent on robotics.
definitions.verification_note: Never adjudicated; the offer was never accepted, so no panel exists

criteria.label: Watch a film and say accurately what is going on
criteria.note: Long-context multimodal models summarise films; reliable plot-twist tracking without confabulation is unshown.

criteria.label: Read a novel and answer questions beyond the literal text
criteria.note: The closest to met. Still below competent-adult reliability on adversarial long-book questions.

criteria.label: Work as a competent cook in an arbitrary kitchen
criteria.note: No general household-capable robot. Marcus later excluded this task from his real bet as too hardware-dependent.

criteria.label: Reliably construct bug-free code of more than 10,000 lines from a natural language specification, or by interacting with a non-expert user
criteria.note: No demonstration at this scale. Marcus's December 2025 review called agents broadly unreliable, though not about this task specifically; markets still price it the likeliest technical task to fall by 2027.

criteria.label: Convert arbitrary proofs from the mathematical literature, written in natural language, into a symbolic form suitable for verification
criteria.note: Whole-paper autoformalisation arrived in 2026: LeanMarathon formalised seven target theorems with no 'sorry' across two research papers. But those were hand-selected, and models still fail to stay faithful when a proof is paraphrased or a value changed.

definitions.name: Eight of ten tasks by end of 2027
definitions.affiliation: Brundage: formerly OpenAI Senior Advisor for AGI Readiness
definitions.quote: Both of us agree that the achievement of 8 out of 10 of these tasks would be strong evidence for the G (General) in Artificial General Intelligence having been achieved. For the purpose of the bet, the tasks should not be performed by 10 completely separate systems.
definitions.quote_source: Marcus & Brundage, 30 December 2024. Accepted, funded and live
definitions.status_today: This is the real wager, and the one that should be cited instead of the Musk offers. Ten tasks, some expected of ordinary adults and some at the limits of the most proficient humans: follow an unseen film including plot twists; read new novels; write NYT-quality obituaries without hallucination; master any new video game in minutes; write legal briefs inventing no cases; 10,000 lines of bug-free code; Pulitzer-calibre books; Oscar-calibre screenplays; Nobel-calibre discoveries; and formalise arbitrary published proofs. Robotics was deliberately excluded. Marcus is heavily favoured, at 88% on Metaculus. The most informative thing about this bet is a factual dispute nobody has adjudicated: Metaculus's crowd rationale says "six out of ten tasks likely solved already," while Marcus's own December 2025 audit says "no system solved more than 4 (or maybe any)." Markets put 22.8% on the bet being annulled, because the panel of judges that decides it still does not publicly exist.
definitions.verification_note: The judging panel that decides it has still not been named

definitions.name: A Turing Test passed by 2029
definitions.affiliation: Long Bets #1, the inaugural Long Now wager
definitions.quote: each of the three Turing Test Judges will conduct online interviews of each of the four Turing Test Candidates for two hours each for a total of eight hours of interviews conducted by each of the three Judges (for a total of 24 hours of interviews)
definitions.quote_source: The Kurzweil–Kapor rules, agreed 2002. Requiring both a Human Determination Test and a Rank Order Test
definitions.status_today: Unresolved and, more interestingly, never attempted. In twenty-four years no committee has been seated and not one interview has been conducted. Meanwhile the capability evidence points hard at Kurzweil: GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time in the 2025 PNAS study. But that was a five-minute conversation with lay participants, and this wager demands 24 hours of interviews per trial across at least three trials. The most telling detail is what forecasters now worry about. Metaculus's question on a long adversarial Turing test lists as its top factor: "Big companies unlikely to run Turing test soon." The probability of the Long Bets version passing before 2030 has fallen roughly 60 points in two years, not on capability pessimism, but on the expectation that nobody will bother to run it.
definitions.verification_note: No committee seated and no interview conducted in 24 years

definitions.name: The Einstein Test: derive general relativity from 1911
definitions.quote: training an AI system with a knowledge cutoff of, say, 1911, and then seeing if it could come up with general relativity like Einstein did in 1915. That's the kind of true test of whether we have a full AGI system.
definitions.quote_source: Demis Hassabis, India AI Impact Summit, 19 February 2026
definitions.status_today: Not met, by Hassabis's own assessment. He added in the same breath that "it's clear today's systems couldn't do that." The nearest real evidence cuts both ways. In May 2026 an internal OpenAI reasoning model disproved the Erdős unit distance conjecture, open since 1946, a result verified by external mathematicians including Tim Gowers and Noga Alon. That is a genuine novel discovery. It is not a paradigm-shifting theory derived from a deliberately impoverished knowledge base. The test may also not be runnable: constructing a genuinely 1911-clean training corpus at frontier scale is an unsolved data-provenance problem, and the mathematical machinery Einstein used predates 1911, making "independent discovery" hard to adjudicate.
definitions.drift: Hassabis is the clearest case of raising the bar while shortening the clock. His long-standing definition was "all the cognitive capabilities humans can", a median-human bar. DeepMind's April 2025 safety paper then anchored planning on "Exceptional AGI" at the 99th percentile; February 2026 added the Einstein Test; July 2026 added physical-world understanding as a necessary condition, which structurally disqualifies text-only models. Over the same period his timeline went from 5–10 years to 2–5.
definitions.verification_note: Never run, and arguably unrunnable, a 1911-clean training corpus is an open problem
